**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Snapshot session cookies after the API reads**

If the client's session cookie has expired, `dashboards.get()` or a chart read can trigger `SupersetClient._renew_credentials()` and replace the session with a newly authenticated one. However, `cookies` was already copied from the old session here, so Chromium receives the expired cookie, redirects to login, and eventually times out waiting for dashboard content despite successful API authentication. Copy the cookies after these API reads so the browser uses the renewed session.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow markdown-only dashboards through the readiness check**

For a valid dashboard containing only markdown components, this selector never appears: markdown blocks are not necessarily inside `.dashboard-component-chart-holder`, as `MEASURE_JS` itself accounts for. Consequently, `check_in_browser()` waits 120 seconds and raises a timeout instead of measuring the markdown. Wait for either supported component type, and handle layouts without measurable components without requiring a chart holder.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make the browser network timeout configurable**

When a dashboard needs more than 120 seconds to load its charts, the browser check always times out, even if the deployment has increased `SUPERSET_API_PLUS_TIMEOUT_READ` for slow queries. `TIMEOUT_MS` is used for navigation and readiness waits but has no environment or call-level override. Read the browser timeout from a `SUPERSET_API_PLUS_*` setting so deployments can tune it without modifying the package, as required by the repository's no-hardcoded-configuration rule.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Carry the client's TLS verification setting into Chromium**

For an HTTPS instance with a self-signed certificate, a client initialized with `verify=False` can authenticate and complete the dashboard/chart API reads, but this new browser context still uses Chromium's default certificate verification. Consequently, `page.goto()` fails with a certificate error instead of returning a report. Honor `self.client.session.verify` when configuring the context's `ignore_https_errors`, while retaining verification by default.
